newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Pope urges unity as bishops row over proselytism.
newsitem.headline: Pope urges unity as bishops row over proselytism.

text.p: Pope John Paul on Tuesday called for unity among Christian churches in a message to a bishops' forum in Graz, southern Austria, where some participants accused rivals of wooing followers away.
"As Christians we must all be deeply convinced of our common responsibility to further respect for human rights, justice and peace and for the sanctity of life," he said.

The Pope, spiritual leader of the world's 960 million Roman Catholics, expressed his regret at the new problems and tensions in Eastern Europe and said that Christians from the East and West could make a "common and yet differentiated" contribution to the spiritual dimension of Europe.
Some 10,000 participants are expected at the Second European Ecumenical Conference which began on Monday and will end on Sunday. The theme of the forum is reconciliation.

Both Patriarch Alexiy II of the Russian Orthodox Church and Karekin I, spiritual leader of the world's Armenian Christians, have voiced sharp criticism at the forum of the missionary work of the Catholic church in Eastern Europe.

Karekin accused "some Western European Churches" of exploiting the chaos following the break-up of the Soviet Union to consolidate their own presence rather than cooperate with the orthodox denominations in the region.

A proposed meeting between Alexiy and the Pope ahead of the conference was called off by the Russian Orthodox Church, which said the churches had failed to agree on important issues that needed to be settled before their heads could meet.
It would have been the first meeting of its kind since the Great Schism split Christendom in 1054.
The first European Ecumenical Conference took place in Basle, Switzerland, in 1989.
